title: Prefetching: what the router asks for unasked
headline: Next's default (fetch every link in view) decides for all but 4 of 947 links, and no test or budget watches it. Re-measured here: a phone shopper who reads the demo store's home page to the footer makes 47 router requests (729 KB decoded) for pages not asked for, 24 of them for the home pages of eight other language, currency and country views; the admin home makes 28; and a multi-country store's front door makes 12 (254 KB) for links whose press loads a whole document anyway. The endless prefetch loop is real but local and CI only (624 router requests in 4 s on the search results page as built, 55 with route guessing off), and one config line stops it. The plan is three changes of a few lines first (the loop, the other views, the links that leave their root layout), then one small link wrapper that states a policy per link group, held by a request budget; none of it argues from an unused feature, and all of it is cheapest before opening.

clean: Storefront prefetch answers are cacheable once rendered (s-maxage 900 s for a home page, 3,600 s otherwise, with stale-while-revalidate), and no link asks for a full dynamic prefetch. They are not static from the start: a store's first ask of each route and view runs a render, and a stale one a background render (the skeptic's correction, kept).
The admin's prefetch answers are prerendered shells without any store's or person's data, and admin paths are outside the proxy's matcher (src/proxy.ts:54-60).
The language switcher of built headers and footers (src/components/language-links.tsx) uses plain anchors and router.push on press: no prefetch.

Search results' tracked product links are plain anchors with nofollow, so a prefetch can never record a click (src/components/product-card.tsx:69-72); export, CSV and print links pass prefetch={false}.

No <Link> points at a route handler: a scan of Link and ButtonLink hrefs for export, csv, pdf, xml, label, feed, download and the like found only pages (the planner's rg); the files themselves are reached by plain anchors or prefetch={false}.

Filter chips and Show more on a listing cost no request: on /s/demo/no/category/hjem?stock=1&min=100&kind=physical the chip links (?min=100, ?stock=1) are in the HTML and the router asked for neither (the planner's run). The same route with other search params shares its shell.

Links inside a closed <details>, a hidden part or display:none do not count as in view, so the header's closed country, language and currency menus and the phone's slide-out menu prefetch nothing until opened.

Prefetched answers live five minutes in the browser's router cache: 70 of 85 cacheLife() calls are the 'hours' profile and nothing sets staleTimes, so soft navigation within a visit does not ask again. Every full page load starts from nothing, which is why PF-4 matters.
The cart link on a phone is prefetching well spent: the tap is one navigation request of 4,859 B and the drawer opens from the prefetched shell.
The @drawer slot follows Next's documented pattern for closing a modal (parallel-routes.md:468-486) and D64 explains it. The loop is the framework's fault, not the route's.

The proxy has to see prefetch requests (it rewrites short addresses and holds the private-store gate, src/proxy.ts:96-151) and reads a store's facts at most every few seconds, never per request. The remedy is fewer prefetches, not skipping the proxy.

Production's store hosts are spared the loop by construction: every /s/ address redirects to the store's host (src/lib/store-hosts.ts:89-104), and route guessing refuses an address that does not spell its route.
The admin's service worker precaches only its offline shell (src/lib/admin-sw.ts:19), and the only resource hint in the app is the font preload (src/components/font-preloads.tsx:25).
No finding in this dimension argues from an unused feature or an empty table. These are costs per page view, per press and per save: they grow with shoppers, owners and stores.

findings.title: Next's route guessing and the cart drawer's catch-all slot make an endless prefetch on the local build and in CI: about 165 requests a second reach the server per open page
findings.evidence: Cause, as the skeptic proved and re-run here. Next 16.4.3 guesses a link's route tree from a route of the same shape it already learned (experimental.optimisticRouting, on by default at config-shared.js:212; cache.js:344 reads the flag that define-env.js:206 sets). The guess fills params from the address along the main branch only, so the rest param of the @drawer/[...rest] slot is never filled, and the code keeps the old value under its own comment "TODO: This should never happen. Bail out with null" (optimistic-routes.js:590-594). The slot's segment is written under one key and read under another, reads Empty, and is asked for again without end. Planner's runs: work/pf/probe.mjs on /s/demo/no/search?q=lampe at 1440x900, 4 s each: 624 router requests as built, 55 with guessing off, 47 with a two-line bail-out (the skeptic on a phone: 495, 23, 21). watch.mjs on /s/demo/no/category/hjem at 1440x900: 2,040 router requests in 5 s, 1,994 of them one address and segment. The skeptic's corrections stand: about 165 a second reach the server (the other half of the request events are answered by the browser's cache); 9 of 11 demo pages never go idle at CI's 1280x720; the trigger is any link whose route shape was learned before its prefetch starts. Behind a rewrite the address does not spell the route, no shape is learned and nothing loops; with the store domain set every /s/ address redirects to the store's host (store-hosts.ts:89-104), so production cannot loop today.
findings.cost: Per looping page (the skeptic's measures): 4.7 s of server CPU per 9 s (0.16 s when quiet), 2.8 s of browser main-thread time per 8 s (0.08 s when quiet), a heap that grows from 3 to 13 MB in 8 s. waitForLoadState('networkidle') never resolves on such a page (e2e/a11y.ts:51 swallows that; 13 spec files wait for it). In production nothing today.
findings.who_pays: CI's e2e job: 25 spec files open /s/demo addresses in 101 goto calls at 1280x720. CI's signed-in job runs without the store domain too, and 12 of its spec files open /s/ addresses (exposed where the store has a country in its address). Anyone running the production build at /s/ addresses. Shoppers would pay only if a later Next release learns shapes through rewrites while the TODO stands: a risk, not a cost.

The NextConfig type (config-shared.d.ts:437) and config-schema.js:246 accept it; define-env.js:206 turns it into the flag cache.js:344 reads.

Create e2e/prefetch.spec.ts with one helper that records every request whose headers carry rsc: 1 and next-router-prefetch (its path and its next-router-segment-prefetch header). findings.title: Every page of a store with several languages, currencies or countries prefetches the home page of each other view, and for languages and currencies the press does not open it
findings.evidence: The standard footer lists the view choices as <Link>s to each view's front page (LocaleChoice as a list at store-layout.tsx:531, countries at 537; a built header's or footer's Countries part at site-parts.tsx:184-208). Each is prefetched when it comes into view: 3 requests a link, the other view's layout (55 KB decoded), its home page (29 KB) and the drawer slot's default (0.6 KB). Re-measured by the planner on the demo store's home page read to the footer on a phone: 8 links, 24 of 47 requests, 662.0 of 729.3 KB decoded, 135.4 of 204.0 KB on the wire; the built /products page shows the same 24 of 48. For the 6 language and currency links the press handler cancels the link and pushes the current page in the chosen view (view-menu.tsx:62-72), so the prefetched home page is used only on the home page. The 2 country links have no handler and do open what was fetched. Only the template store's views are built ahead (shop.ts:93-101), so on a real store the first prefetch of a view renders its layout and home page (75 to 78 ms cold per the skeptic), and again when stale (s-maxage 900).
findings.cost: Per page view that reaches the footer: 24 requests and 662 KB decoded in the browser, 24 proxy runs, and up to 8 server renders of pages nobody opened when the cache is cold or stale. A built header that shows the Countries part as a list pays it at the top of every page. On a store host each link also asks for its route tree: about 32 requests (the skeptic's estimate from the mechanism).
findings.who_pays: The shopper's browser and data plan; the proxy and the server per request. Only stores with Several languages, Several currencies or several countries pay, but every page view of theirs does, whether or not a shopper ever switches. It grows with stores times views.

findings.title: The header tools, bottom bar and footer are prefetched on every full page load, with the script chunks of pages nobody asked for
findings.evidence: Each link costs a route-tree request plus one per segment not yet held. Planner's runs on the demo store: a phone at the top of the home page, 11 router requests for 4 links (search 3, wishlist 3, cart 3, account 2); at the top of a product page, 12 (40.3 KB on the wire: the home page behind the logo and the bottom bar is the largest, 3 requests and 29.6 KB decoded); at 1440x900, 17 for 7 links. Read to the footer on a phone: cookies 2, withdraw 2, the footer menu's four links 8. The skeptic's addition stands: the answers name script chunks the router then loads (3 chunks, 24 KB on the wire at the top; 10 chunks, 87 KB read to the footer), and 10 of 18 routes answered STALE, each a background render. Every full load starts again from nothing. Next's own guide gives the pattern for links that should wait for intent (prefetching.md:121-156): prefetch={active ? null : false}, switched on by the pointer. A link with prefetch={false} is not prefetched on hover either (links.js:134-165, 236-249), which is why the wrapper must flip the prop. The 'checkout, 50 requests' of the first report was a checkout that bounces to the cart; no pay step was measured.
findings.cost: Per full page load on a phone: 11 to 12 router requests and 3 script chunks at the top (about 55 KB on the wire here); 23 router requests with the footer (other views left to PF-2). One proxy run each; on a quiet store a render per route when cold and one per hour or quarter hour when stale.
findings.who_pays: The shopper's browser; the proxy and the server per request. It grows with page views across all stores, whatever features they use.

findings.title: The links shoppers press most on built pages are full page loads: a whole document and every prefetch made again where one small answer would do
findings.evidence: The page builder's blocks link with plain anchors: the content grid's tile title, picture and button (content-grid.tsx:147, 226-236, 304, 310), icon lists (icon-list-view.tsx:48), the link over a column (page-parts.tsx:448-458) and, opened by the planner, the button, dual button, picture and video blocks too (page-block.tsx:180, 246, 302, 366). The demo's home page and its /products page are built pages: the planner's fetch of /s/demo/no/products shows its nine tiles as plain <a> and the router asked for none of them. The skeptic's measure on a phone: a tap on a home page tile is a document load of 42 requests and 104.5 KB on the wire (document 24.0 KB, 12 prefetches made again 40.3 KB, scripts 33.5 KB); a <Link> press to a product page from the same page is 5 requests and 12.9 KB. Soft navigation away from a built page is not new: menus are <Link>s and rich text already draws internal addresses with <Link> (rich-text.tsx:83-86). No rule or decision says why the blocks differ. findings.title: Partial Prefetching was planned, never switched on, and the next major Next release forces it
findings.evidence: The plan's stack line reads cacheComponents + partialPrefetching (docs/plan.md:120); the config sets only cacheComponents (next.config.ts:42). Every start logs that the option is unset and that both will be on everywhere in the next major release (start.log:8-14, read here). From Next's docs, not measured (no build was allowed): a default link then fetches one App Shell per route, shared by all links to that route, and content that depends on params or searchParams comes after the press unless the link passes prefetch={true}. For this app: admin rows and the links to one route collapse to one fetch per route (the 18 links of the home page are 11 routes, the skeptic's count), but every storefront page depends on the store and market params, which the market layout reads at its top (layout.tsx:105), so by default almost nothing of a store page would be fetched ahead. A segment can opt in alone with export const prefetch = 'partial' (prefetch.md:39-45).
findings.cost: Today: the duplicate shells of PF-6 and one prefetch per link everywhere, and a warning in every build and start log. Later: a forced migration on Next's date, with shoppers watching.
findings.who_pays: Shoppers' and owners' browsers now; the team at the next major upgrade.

findings.title: Links that leave their root layout are fetched ahead, and pressing them loads a whole document anyway: a multi-country store's front door fetches every country's home page for nothing
findings.evidence: Missed by the report. The app has 14 root layouts (layout.tsx files that draw <html>, and platform-root.tsx:65 for the platform groups): a store's front door (s/[store]/(chooser)) and its market pages (s/[store]/[market]) are two of them, the admin a third, Kaizena Flow's own pages a fourth. Next's docs: navigating across root layouts causes a full page load (layout.md:145). The links between them are <Link>s all the same, so they are prefetched. Measured by the planner at 1440x900. The demo store's front door /s/demo: 12 router requests for its 3 country links, 254 KB decoded, 58.6 KB on the wire (each: the route tree, the market layout 54.7 KB, the home page 28.8 KB, the drawer's default); all 12 answered STALE. Pressing Denmark then loaded a document (21,354 B) and 56 more requests: nothing fetched ahead was used. findings.title: The first add to cart of a visit throws the router's whole prefetch cache away: 20 more requests on a phone, at the moment the shopper buys
findings.evidence: Missed by the report, which read the mechanism for the admin and did not measure it. A cart is made on the first add, and making it sets the cart's cookie (cart.ts:698-726). Next answers a server action that changed a cookie as one that revalidated static and dynamic data (action-handler.js:123-126), and the router then evicts the entire prefetch cache and asks again for every link in view (server-action-reducer.js:228-229; cache.js:270-274; links.js:285-306); Next's own comment there says the eviction is wider than it should be. Measured by the planner twice, with the same numbers, on /s/demo/no/p/demo-handlenett on a phone at the top of the page (work/pfplan/addcart2.mjs): the load made 12 router prefetch requests (40.3 KB on the wire); the first press of Add to cart made 32 more request events, 20 of them on the network (28.9 KB), and its answer carried x-action-revalidated: 1. The second press carried 2 (dynamic only) and asked for nothing. At 1440x900 the first add asked again for 12 links (one of them inside PF-1's loop). The same eviction follows the buyer switch (b2b.ts:46 sets a cookie, and buyer.tsx then calls router.refresh() too), a customer's sign-in (customers.ts:416), and every admin save whose action revalidates.
findings.cost: Once per visit that adds to a cart: 20 requests on the network on a phone at the top of a product page, more with the footer in view (every link in view is asked again). Each is a proxy run, and they share the phone's connection with the action's own refresh of the page.
findings.who_pays: The shopper's browser at the moment of buying; the proxy and the server per request. It grows with carts started.
fix_steps: No change to the cart: the cookie has to be set when the cart is made (D14: the one cookie a cart has), and the eviction is Next's. The cost is the number of links in view, so PF-2, PF-3 and PF-7 remove most of it: on a phone only the cart link keeps viewport prefetch.

e2e/prefetch.spec.ts: add 'the first add to cart asks for little again': on a phone at the top of /s/demo/no/p/demo-handlenett, count router prefetch requests in the 4 s after the first press of the add button: at most 10 (32 today). A second press: 0.

docs/performance.md, 'What the router fetches ahead': one sentence that a server action which sets a cookie or revalidates makes the router ask again for every link in view, so the count of viewport-prefetched links is also the cost of every such action, in the store and in the admin.
tests_and_rules: e2e/cart.spec.ts, e2e/shop-components.spec.ts (Add to cart on tiles, D557), e2e/b2b.spec.ts (the buyer switch) and e2e/account.spec.ts (sign-in) exercise the actions: behaviour is unchanged.
D14 (the cart's one strictly necessary cookie) stays as it is.
findings.done_when: e2e/prefetch.spec.ts 'the first add to cart asks for little again' passes: at most 10 router prefetch request events after the first add on a phone (32 today, 20 of them on the network).
findings.saving: Estimate from the measured list: from 32 request events (20 on the network) to the cart link's own, 7 events in my run (its tree, the market layout, its default and the drawer page, some asked twice).
findings.risk: None of its own: nothing changes but a test and a sentence.
findings.notes: Not worth a change of its own beyond the budget case: minting the cart outside a server action (a route handler) would be a larger change for 20 requests once a visit. Worth reporting upstream with PF-1: Next's TODO at server-action-reducer.js:223-227 describes the narrower eviction.

findings.title: A real listing prefetches every product tile, and up to six swatch links under each: nothing bounds it, and the test stores are too small to show it
findings.evidence: Missed by the report because the test data cannot show it. The demo and test stores have 10 products each (counted in the local database), and the demo's /products and home pages are built pages whose tiles are plain anchors (PF-4), so no measurement of this review saw a real listing. A category, tag, brand or related-products listing draws ProductCard, whose title is a <Link> with no policy (product-card.tsx:74), up to 48 a page (LISTING_LIMIT, listing.ts:59), and Show more adds 48 at a time up to 20 pages (listing.ts:207). Measured by the planner per product link (the three in the header's menu, on /s/demo/no/products at 1440x900): 2 requests, the route tree (1,035 B decoded, 2.4 KB on the wire) and the product page's shell (10.1 to 10.5 KB decoded, 5.1 KB on the wire). A combined listing (D566) adds up to 6 swatch <Link>s under each card (product-card.tsx:96-118), each to another product page. Only the template store is built ahead (shop.ts:93-101), so the first ask of each product in each view renders its shell (75 to 78 ms cold, the skeptic's measure) and a stale one renders in the background (s-maxage 3,600 s).
findings.cost: Estimate by multiplication, not measured: a 48-tile listing read to the end is 96 requests, about 360 KB on the wire and 550 KB decoded, and up to 48 shell renders when the store has been quiet for an hour; with swatches up to 288 more links. Filter chips and Show more cost nothing (checked, see clean).
findings.who_pays: The shopper's browser on every listing; the proxy and the server (a render per product seen on a quiet store). It grows with stores times catalogue size, which is what opening brings.
